definition: Audiometry here refers to the use of evoked response audiometry systems to measure auditory brain responses, such as the 40-Hz auditory steady-state response. In this context, it is described as a widely available and practical method for individual-level assessment in psychiatric research.

reasons: The packet does not support the claim that evoked response audiometry (ERA) systems are “widely available” and “practical” for individual-level assessment; it only states that “clinically scalable methods … remain limited” and that “widely available” ERA systems offer a “pragmatic and accessible platform,” but does not specifically establish practical/availability for individual-level assessment as a general method.

The definition’s framing as a “widely available and practical method for individual-level assessment in psychiatric research” is broader than what the packet explicitly demonstrates; the packet describes utility and investigates extension to mood disorders, but does not explicitly claim broad individual-level assessment capability.

The packet supports measuring the 40-Hz auditory steady-state response with ERA and notes utility in schizophrenia, but it does not explicitly support the overall “in this context” characterization as a diagnosis field method beyond the biomarker/research framing.
